# Introduction

# Preparations

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
theme_set(hrbrthemes::theme_ipsum_rc())
```

```{r}
lm_with_scatter <- function(logx = TRUE, logy = FALSE) {
  l <- list(
    geom_point(size = 0.3),
    geom_smooth(color = "tomato", method = "lm")
  )
  labs <- scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())
  if (logx) l <- append(l, scale_x_log10(labels = labs))
  if (logy) l <- append(l, scale_y_log10(labels = labs))
  l
}

par(
  pch = 19,
  cex = 0.8,
  bty = "n"
)
```

# Getting the data

A relatively clean dataset with information on population size, GDP, and employment across a variety of sectors has been compiled from the OECD Data Explorer in the `build/build-dataset.R` script.

```{r}
dat <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb("../data/processed/data.parquet")
```

# Getting to know the data

```{}
 1 M_N      Professional, scientific and technical activities; administrative a…
 2 L        Real estate activities
 3 J        Information and communication
 4 _T       Total - all activities
 5 C        Manufacturing
 6 OTQ      Public administration, defence, education, human health and social …
 7 A        Agriculture, forestry and fishing
 8 K        Financial and insurance activities
 9 GTI      Wholesale and retail trade; repair of motor vehicles and motorcycle…
10 F        Construction
11 RTU      Arts, entertainment and recreation; other service activities; activ…
12 BTE      Industry (except construction)
```

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
dat <- dat |>
  mutate(
    finance = emp_K / emp__T,
    ict = emp_J / emp__T,
    proftech = emp_M_N / emp__T,
    pubadmin = emp_OTQ / emp__T,
    realest = emp_L / emp__T,
    trade_vehicles = emp_GTI / emp__T,
    construction = emp_F / emp__T,
    entertainment = emp_RTU / emp__T,
    industry = emp_BTE / emp__T,
    manufact = emp_C / emp__T,
    agricult = emp_A / emp__T
  )
```

# Urban scaling

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
countries <- c("USA", "DEU", "FRA", "ITA", "NLD", "POL")

pd <- filter(dat, time == 2020, country %in% countries)

p1 <- ggplot(filter(pd, country == "USA"), aes(pop, gdp)) +
  lm_with_scatter(logx = TRUE, logy = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Extensive GDP (total)")

p2 <- ggplot(filter(pd, country == "USA"), aes(pop, gdp_pc)) +
  lm_with_scatter(logx = TRUE, logy = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Intensive GDP (per capita)")

p1 | p2
```

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(pd, aes(pop, gdp_pc)) +
  lm_with_scatter(logx = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~country, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Cross-country comparison")
```
